content.title: About
content.content: A classic dish featuring tender beef, boiled or roasted potatoes, and a mix of vegetables – carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy greens (spinach, kale). Served with a savory gravy that ties all components together.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef is one of the most widely consumed sources of animal protein worldwide.
Potatoes were introduced to Europe from South America in the 16th century and have become a staple food.
Broccoli belongs to the cruciferous family, along with cabbage, cauliflower and Brussels sprouts.
Carrots are rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Dark‑green leafy vegetables provide high amounts of vitamin K, essential for blood clotting.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Beef supplies all essential amino acids needed for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef is a good source of B12, niacin and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Potassium and magnesium
items.content: Potatoes and leafy greens are rich in potassium, which helps regulate blood pressure, while magnesium supports muscle function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Broccoli and carrots contain vitamin C and carotenoids that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Vegetables and potatoes (especially with skin) provide fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Saturated fat intake
items.content: Fatty cuts of beef can raise cholesterol levels if consumed excessively.

items.title: Sodium in gravy
items.content: Prepared gravies often contain high salt; monitor the amount added.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Rare, but some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to beef.

items.title: Potential pathogens
items.content: Undercooked beef may harbor bacteria such as E. coli or salmonella; cook to an internal temperature of at least 63 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice beef into bite‑size pieces and sear or braise until tender. Boil, bake, or roast potatoes. Steam, blanch or lightly sauté carrots, broccoli and greens to retain crunch and nutrients. Drizzle the gravy over the assembled plate just before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh beef refrigerated at +2–4 °C for 3–5 days or freeze at ‑18 °C for up to 6 months. Store potatoes in a cool, dark place and vegetables in the fridge in airtight containers. Gravy should be kept in a sealed jar in the refrigerator and used within 5 days.
